title: Army Weekly Briefing
description: Army leadership, force design, modernization, contracts and the signal and network enterprise.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 23–29. No Army contract, leadership confirmation, or NETCOM release dated Oct. 28–29 was found. The Oct. 26 Project Griffin pilot and the USAISEC wide-area-network replacement remain the newest items. An Oct. 14 Army xTech announcement still lists white papers for a Europe spectrum-warfare challenge as closing Oct. 30; no newer Army release on that challenge was found.

items.headline: MeriTalk: Army selected AWS and WWT for a $2.6 million Project Griffin pilot
items.summary: MeriTalk reported Oct. 26 that the Army selected Amazon Web Services and World Wide Technology for a combined $2.6 million pilot under Project Griffin, aimed at AI-enabled cyber defense. MeriTalk says Griffin is one of three accelerated efforts under Project ARDS, the Army Rapid Defensive of Cyber Systems initiative, and that the aim is an autonomous, agentic platform so defenders can identify and neutralize threats faster and cut vulnerabilities tied to manual analysis. Principal cyber advisor Brandon Pugh said Griffin is one of the first ARDS efforts and that the Army will implement what he called SI-enabled tools to detect, divert and deceive threat actors. MeriTalk also says the administration has directed agencies to call AI super intelligence, or SI, in official documents.

items.headline: USAISEC, with NETCOM, is replacing Army wide-area network gear in the U.S. and Europe
items.summary: An Army.mil article datelined Aberdeen Proving Ground on Oct. 26 says the U.S. Army Information Systems Engineering Command, a Communications-Electronics Command subordinate, is leading lifecycle replacement of wide-area network equipment across the United States and Europe in coordination with Network Enterprise Technology Command. The article says the work is meant to produce one software-defined enterprise network, using software-defined wide-area network technology and next-generation firewalls so the network can shift around outages, congestion and cyber threats without manual intervention. It says the design is a zero-trust model and that USAISEC engineers check power, cooling and shielding before new hardware goes in. Director of the Data Science and Engineering Directorate Dr. Jennifer Mills said the switches, servers and firewalls are the bedrock of the Army's digital future. USAISEC is headquartered at Fort Huachuca and uses hubs at Fort Huachuca and Fort Gordon.

items.headline: Army says Project Gatekeeper, its commercial-software security sandbox, launched Oct. 23
items.summary: Army Public Affairs said Oct. 25 that the Office of the Chief Information Officer launched Project Gatekeeper on Oct. 23, a DevSecOps platform and security-evaluation sandbox for commercial software. Acting CIO Gabe Chiulli said the automated intake is meant to cut evaluation cycles from months to minutes while keeping the network perimeter in place. The release says vendors submit code and containerized applications into isolated enclaves that do not expose operational data, and that the pipelines produce evidence dossiers for an authority to operate. Access is currently limited to a Department of War common access card, with public Login.gov access described as coming later, and the release says the platform will later use frontier security models from unnamed super intelligence partners.
